analysis.title: High Grade Copper Futures: FCI Tightening vs Potential Tariffs
key_insights: Commitment of Traders for Nov 3-10 showed the 7th straight week of speculative selling in High Grade Copper futures. Managed Money, Other, and Non-Reportable sold $1.3bn, bringing the running total since Sep 22 to $10.8bn. Other was the main driver, with a sizeable uptick in shorts.

Producer / Processor / Merchant / User (PMPU) remained the dominant bull, buying $1.1bn net, half of it gross long additions. PMPU gross longs as a percentage of total open interest reached a new multiyear max.
Between Nov 10 and Nov 17, High Grade Copper fell 4.1%. GS's US Financial Conditions Index tightened after inflation data and Fed speak, and Data Centers slipped 3.2%.
Per the GS Futures Strategists framework, medium-term momentum turned negative, which prompted significant CTA sell estimates.
The option surface showed impaired long-term sentiment: High Grade Copper 1 year normalized 25 delta put-call skew reached a 99% 1 year rank.
GS says PMPU's resolve in waiting for potential tariff signaling seems crucial. It notes this category could not withstand a geopolitical reversal in Brent Oil over the past few weeks.
risk_factors: Further tightening of financial conditions, as GS's US FCI tightened after inflation data and Fed speak
Further CTA selling after the medium-term momentum flip
PMPU capitulation if tariff signaling does not arrive

tension_points.theme: copper tariffs vs tighter financial conditions
tension_points.bull_case: PMPU remained the dominant bull, net buying $1.1bn with gross longs as a share of open interest at a new multiyear max, waiting for potential tariff signaling.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions and Data Center weakness cut copper 4.1%, medium-term momentum turned negative with significant CTA sell estimates, and skew shows a 99% 1 year rank for puts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: PMPU's resolve giving way without tariff signaling, as it did under the geopolitical reversal in Brent Oil in recent weeks.
